encounters.cc: Two weeks of hard stools and straining with defecation; infant appears fussy during bowel movements.

lines: Two weeks of hard stools and straining with defecation; infant appears fussy during bowel movements.
The patient, a male infant with Osteogenesis imperfecta Type III and conductive hearing loss, returns to the pediatric clinic following recovery from infant botulism diagnosed in April 2020.
He is brought to the pediatrician by his mother, who reports that her son has been having difficulty with bowel movements for the past two weeks.
She notes that his stools are hard and that he seems to strain and become fussy when attempting to defecate.
The infant was exclusively breastfed until 6 months of age, at which point solid foods were introduced.
His diet consists of rice cereal, pureed fruits and vegetables, and continued breastfeeding.
The mother denies any fever, vomiting, blood in the stool, or significant abdominal distension.

lines: Preschool-age assessment for bone health; mother reports several fractures over past year including recent femur fracture after falling from sitting position.
The patient is a 4-year-old male with established Osteogenesis imperfecta Type III who returns for continued orthopedic monitoring and assessment of his pamidronate therapy.

The mother denies any known trauma, rough handling, or delay in seeking care.
She states that he has always seemed “a bit more fragile” than other children.
Developmental milestones are normal for age.
